cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Group cash is not split by listed parent/offshore/PRC operating entities; business is PRC education with prepaid/refund obligations, so use the conservative end of PRC subsidiary/group-cash haircut rather than full deduction.
cash_breakdown.reason: Bank demand deposits and licensed payment institution cash are fund assets, but only part can be treated as realistically detachable without disrupting operations.

cash_breakdown.item: Current USD term deposits with initial term over three months
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Short-duration USD term deposits are closer to detachable treasury assets, but cash location and repatriation path are not fully disclosed.
cash_breakdown.reason: Current term deposits are surplus treasury assets according to management's treasury policy disclosure.

cash_breakdown.item: Non-current RMB term deposits with initial term over three months
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Non-current RMB deposits are longer dated and likely tied to PRC treasury arrangements; distribution path to controlling shareholder is not proven.
cash_breakdown.reason: Term deposits are fund assets but not immediate operating cash.

cash_breakdown.item: Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Wealth management products are largely non-guaranteed variable/fixed return products and Level 3 fair value assets, so use mid-low FVTPL wealth-management haircut.
cash_breakdown.reason: Management says these are surplus-cash financial products, but product risk and liquidity are weaker than cash or bank deposits.

cash_breakdown.item: Other financial assets at amortised cost
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Short-term note has guaranteed return and no historical default disclosed, but was extended to 2026 and is a single counterparty credit exposure.
cash_breakdown.reason: Short-term note is an idle-fund investment and can enter the detachable pool only with credit/liquidity haircut.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Restricted cash is not detachable under the screening rule.
cash_breakdown.reason: Reported as restricted cash in the balance sheet and cash-flow note.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Approximately two months of cash operating costs after excluding depreciation/amortisation and share-based payments; protects course delivery, refunds, payroll and marketing volatility.
cash_breakdown.reason: 2025 expenses by nature were RMB2.515bn, with venue leases, employee costs and prepaid course/refund obligations requiring liquidity.

cash_breakdown.item: Tax, FX and distribution friction reserve
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Cash is held across RMB, USD and HKD with PRC operations and no proven immediate parent-level distribution path; reserve covers withholding tax, FX and dividend friction.
cash_breakdown.reason: Annual report notes foreign exchange exposure and deferred withholding tax for distributed profits.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: No bank loans or other borrowings were outstanding at 2025 year-end.
cash_breakdown.reason: No financing debt deduction is needed for borrowings.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: These are continuing operating venue leases, not cash raised against detachable financial assets; the recurring lease burden is reflected in cash-profit quality rather than deducted as acquisition debt.
cash_breakdown.reason: Classroom and office leases are necessary for continuing operations.

profit_quality.assessment: Usable but not pristine. 2025 operating cash flow covered reported profit, and capex is low, but the business is facing low-price competition, uses leased venues, carries prepaid course and refund obligations, and reported profit includes treasury income that would disappear if funds are stripped.
adjustments: Start from 2023-2025 profit record: RMB188.6m, RMB239.6m and RMB198.1m; the three-year median is RMB198.1m.
Remove treasury return and fair-value contribution from the operating-business earnings base: 2025 finance income net was RMB33.3m and FVTPL fair value gains were RMB9.5m before tax.
Do not add back share-based payments for owner cash profit, because they are non-cash in accounting but represent employee compensation and dilution economics.
Treat 2025 capex of RMB9.1m and lease principal payments of about RMB60.8m as relevant cash burdens for a venue-based education business.

Use RMB160.0m as pre-haircut sustainable distributable cash profit, then apply a 0.75 cash-profit haircut for competition, refund/prepaid-course obligations and incomplete multi-year cash-flow extraction.
profit_quality.cashflow_support: 2025 operating cash flow was RMB226.3m versus profit of RMB198.1m; after RMB9.1m capex and RMB60.8m lease principal, a rough lease-adjusted free cash figure is about RMB156.4m, close to the RMB160.0m pre-haircut base.
profit_quality.haircut_reason: Cash conversion is acceptable in 2025, but the denominator deserves a material haircut because revenue declined, AI-course commercialization raises marketing/R&D spend, refund liabilities remain material, and only the 2025 filing was deeply extracted for cash-flow detail.
profit_quality.cash_conversion_assessment: 2025 operating cash flow / reported net profit was about 1.14x, but working-capital movements were negative and lease principal is outside operating cash flow under IFRS.
profit_quality.maintenance_capex_assessment: 2025 capex was RMB9.1m, low relative to revenue; venue use is mostly through leases rather than owned fixed assets.
profit_quality.working_capital_assessment: Working capital consumed cash in 2025 through lower payables, lower contract/refund liabilities and higher receivables/prepayments.
